metadata.case_name: YIP MAU KEI v. WONG KAM TIM

plaintiff.occupation_before: night-shift taxi driver for about 10 years prior to the 1st Accident

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to his back (back sprain)
source: the plaintiff as a result of the 1st Accident had suffered a soft tissue injury to his back, and there were only residual back symptoms with mild adverse effects.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

injuries.description: mild degenerative changes of the lower lumbar spine (mild lumbar spondylosis / long standing disc degeneration)
source: an x-ray of the lumbar spine was taken. The plaintiff was found to have mild degenerative changes with marginal osteophytosis in the lower lumbar spine. Dr Lee and Dr Lam both agreed that such features were compatible with mild lumber spondylosis.
the records of the MRI scans done in January 2012 show that there was dehydration of intervertebral discs and mild disc space narrowing of L4/5 , which were due to long standing disc degeneration.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: On and off low back pain
Episodic bilateral big toe numbness, more on left
Could stand and walk on tiptoes or heels, with complaint of back discomfort (gait)
Tenderness at bilateral paraspinal muscles at lower lumbar
Sensory 30% loss in anterior thigh; 20% in rest of whole limb

treatments_received.treatment: Treated and discharged from Queen Elizabeth Hospital; 2 days' sick leave
source: he was treated and discharged with 2 days’ sick leave.
the plaintiff was diagnosed as having sustained a back sprain and soft tissue injuries to the back. Medication was prescribed for his back pain.
In addition, the plaintiff also received three sessions of physiotherapy between March and April 2012.

treatments_received.treatment: Intramuscular analgesic and intensive inpatient physiotherapy (admitted and discharged 29 December 2012)
source: According to the report from Baptist, the plaintiff was found to have tenderness over his lumbar spine region and was given intramuscular analgesic for his pain. He was admitted and discharged on 29 December 2012 during which stay he was given medicine for his pain and provided with intensive inpatient physiotherapy.

treatments_received.treatment: X-ray and MRI imaging of lumbar spine
source: an x-ray taken on that day showed that there was no fracture.
an x-ray of the lumbar spine was taken. The plaintiff was found to have mild degenerative changes with marginal osteophytosis in the lower lumbar spine.
the records of the MRI scans done in January 2012 show that there was dehydration of intervertebral discs and mild disc space narrowing of L4/5 , which were due to long standing disc degeneration.

losses.description: Residual back symptoms with mild adverse effects and reduced work efficiency
